answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Log each identity's action timing, choice distribution, and network neighbors; cluster after the fact. Identities whose traces sit on the same low-entropy ledge of behavior—near-identical sequences across contexts—get merged, voiding their separate rewards. An attacker must make each clone behaviorally distinct: varied timing, independent strategy, its own network oasis of contacts. That raises the per-identity cost to sustained divergent behavior, since a cheap inlet of copied actions gets caught and collapsed.
